text:
Priya Patel: Quick announce — were launching a 4-week pilot for a Temporal Overage Smoothing program on the hosted API. Goal: reduce noisy single-minute/hour spikes showing up as overages on monthly invoices. This is a billing reconciliation experiment, not a rate-limit change. :sparkles:

Maya Chen: How does smoothing work?

Priya Patel: Smoothing aggregates token usage into short windows (1h by default) and applies a small buffer before considering it an overage. If a customer exceeds their monthly allotment only because of narrow spikes that fall inside buffer windows, the excess will be credited on the invoice as `temporal_overage_credit`.

Omar Reyes: So runtime/rate limiter stays the same? Any impact on autoscaling signals?

Priya Patel: Correct — runtime and RL remain unchanged. Autoscaling and SRE alerts are unaffected; smoothing runs in billing reconciliation after data is finalized. Well surface a tag in telemetry so ops can filter out waived spikes when investigating capacity.

Leah Kim: Will customers see anything different on the invoice? Transparency is key for support.

Priya Patel: Yes — invoice will include both the raw usage line and the smoothing credit line. Example stub: 
```
line_item: tokens_used_generation
units: 2,345,678
charge: $234.56
line_item: temporal_overage_credit
units: -4,321
credit: -$0.43
```
Net charge will reflect credit. We will also add a reasoning code in the invoice metadata (customer-visible).

Maya Chen: Eligibility rules?

Priya Patel: Pilot rules: 1) only hosted API (no Dedicated/Private), 2) must be on Standard or higher (Starter excluded), 3) smoothing applies if the excess is caused by <6 windows in a billing period and each window <10% of monthly baseline. Full rules in pilot doc. Customers will be notified before being included and can opt out.

Omar Reyes: Any fraud or abuse concerns? Could this be gamed by traffic shaping?

Priya Patel: We considered that. The reconciliation job includes anomaly heuristics: sustained multi-day overages, repeated patterning, or correlated regional spikes will disqualify a customer from smoothing. Finance has the right to revert credits on review.

Leah Kim: Support ask: prepare a short FAQ and a triage checklist: 1) check smoothing eligibility flag 2) review invoice lines 3) escalate to billing if suspicious.

Priya Patel: Timeline: pilot start = 1857600000 (next Monday), duration 28 days. Billing will send pre-eligibility emails 3 days before inclusion. Pilot docs + QA checklist to be published to the console docs and internal ops page.

Maya Chen: Action items: Priya -> publish customer FAQ & invoice examples; Omar -> add `billing_smoothing_tag` to telemetry; Eng -> ensure console shows provisional credits in the billing preview; Leah -> prep support runbook.

Billing Bot: Recorded: Temporal Overage Smoothing pilot | start=1857600000 | duration=28d | doc=https://internal.redwood/billing/temporal-smoothing-pilot. Will post weekly pilot metrics. :robot_face:

Priya Patel: Thanks team 2 — will post the public announcement draft for review later today. :memo:
